title: Elon Musk Delivered Massive News for Taiwan Semiconductor Stock Investors
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA revisits Taiwan Semiconductor after Elon Musk confirmed on X (Saturday Oct 3) that SpaceX and Tesla are in discussions with TSMC over the Terrafab manufacturing facilities — a blow to Intel, which had been positioned as the likely sole provider. Per a Motley Fool article he cites, two structures are possible: TSMC builds and runs a new fab with SpaceX/Tesla investing and committing to buy output, or SpaceX takes the majority stake while TSMC contributes technology and operating know-how. Either way, it's TSMC's proprietary manufacturing skill Musk is after. He restates that TSMC is "the best manufacturing company in the world, period," noting Intel's appeal was being US-based with spare capacity, while TSMC is sold out with more customers than it can serve. Financially: record 34% ROIC, trailing operating margins of 55.8–56% (57% forecast next quarter), Q3 revenue expected +37% YoY. Long-term margin pressure from less-profitable US/Japan/Europe fabs is known, but elevated utilization keeps beating management's warnings. He also compares TSMC with Micron: Micron likely wins near-term (12–24 months), TSMC over a 15-year horizon. Calls: TSM — BUY (reiteration) — DCF fair value $670 vs ~$484 market price, forward PE ~22; none of the Terrafab upside is in his numbers. No explicit Intel call; SpaceX/Tesla discussed only as potential partners.

calls.thesis: Reiterates BUY: TSMC is "the best manufacturing company in the world, period" — sold-out capacity, record 34% ROIC, 55.8% trailing operating margins (57% forecast next quarter), Q3 revenue expected +37% YoY. SpaceX/Tesla Terrafab fab talks (Musk confirmed on X Oct 3) are pure upside not in his numbers. DCF fair value $670 vs ~$484.
calls.base_case: DCF fair value $670 (~38% upside); forward PE ~22 looks attractive given how much the business has improved.
calls.bull_case: Terrafab deal lands — TSMC builds/operates a new fab with SpaceX/Tesla committing to buy output; adds to Apple/Nvidia/AMD customer base; full utilization keeps margins expanding.
calls.bear_case: Geographic diversification is less profitable (US/Japan/Europe fabs cost more than Taiwan); management warns long-term margins will compress; Intel could win the Terrafab deal as the US-based option.
